title: How to Switch from Reprise to Storylane
summary: Moving from Reprise to Storylane? This guide covers what happens to your demos, the exact migration steps, and what changes after you switch.
body_markdown:
If you're on Reprise and considering a switch, this guide covers what migration actually looks like: what happens to your existing demos, the steps involved, and what your team gains on the other side.


## Why teams move from Reprise to Storylane


If you're still comparing options, our[interactive demo software pricing guide](https://www.storylane.io/blog/interactive-demo-software-pricing) breaks down Reprise, Storylane, and the main alternatives by true cost and use-case fit.


If you've already decided to move, the most common reasons teams make the switch are:


- **Engineering dependency slows everything down.** Building and updating demos in Reprise typically requires technical support. Teams report demo builds taking weeks, not days, and every product UI change creates a maintenance backlog that the engineering or solutions engineering team has to absorb.
- **Onboarding takes months, not days.** Reprise onboarding often involves professional services engagements that stretch across weeks or months. For teams that want to be demoing live quickly, that timeline is a blocker before any value is realized.
- **Maintenance compounds as the product evolves.** Keeping demos current in Reprise is resource-intensive. When your product UI changes, existing demos require significant rework. Teams that ship product updates frequently find the maintenance overhead grows faster than they can manage it.
- **Pricing is opaque, with significant hidden costs.** Reprise's pricing is not publicly listed, and professional services and ongoing support often carry significant add-on fees. Teams that expected a standard SaaS tool frequently find the total cost of ownership higher than anticipated.
- **The platform is built for SE teams, not full-funnel use.** Reprise excels at live product overlay demos for solutions engineers. It's not designed for self-serve marketing embeds, lead capture, or the kind of full-funnel coverage that covers awareness, sales, and post-sales in one tool.


## What happens to your existing Reprise demos?


Your demos carry over. Share the links with Storylane, the screens get captured and rebuilt, and a CSM reviews the migrated demos with you. For anything that relied on Reprise's overlay customization, your CSM helps recreate those elements natively before anything goes live.


## Step-by-step: switching from Reprise to Storylane


**1. Audit your current Reprise demos**


List the demos currently in use: which are embedded on your site, shared in sales sequences, or used live in calls. These are your migration priorities. Older or one-off demos can wait.


**2. Start a Storylane trial or book a migration call**


Sign up at storylane.io or book a demo directly. If you have multiple active demos, the migration call is faster. Storylane's team handles the heavy lifting and your CSM is assigned from the start.


**3. Send your Reprise demo links**


Share the URLs. Storylane's automation captures your screens and rebuilds the guided steps in your workspace. For demos that rely heavily on Reprise's overlay customization, your CSM will work with you to recreate those elements natively in Storylane.


**4. Review and improve with your CSM**


Your CSM walks through the migrated demos with you. This is where you add branching, set up[lead capture forms](https://www.storylane.io/blog/lead-forms-in-storylane-capturing-your-most-promising-leads) , enable[viewer identification and CRM routing](https://www.storylane.io/blog/guide-to-lead-attribution-for-interactive-demos) , and adapt flows previously built for live delivery into self-serve experiences.


**5. Replace your embeds and go live**


Swap the Reprise links for Storylane's. Storylane supports[embedding across your full go-to-market stack](https://www.storylane.io/blog/product-demos-on-multiple-platforms) : website, email sequences, sales decks, LinkedIn outreach, and review sites like G2. Demos that only existed in your SE team's live call rotation can now run 24/7 on your site.


## What you gain after switching


- **No engineering dependency.** Storylane is built for marketers, sales teams, and customer success teams to operate without developer support. Demo creation, updates, and publishing happen inside a no-code builder. When your product UI changes, your team updates the demo, not the engineering queue.
- **Self-serve and sales call coverage in one tool.** The same demo your SE team uses live can be embedded on your website for self-serve access, gated with a lead form, and tracked at the account level. You stop managing separate tools for separate use cases.
- **Branching for every buyer path.** Build one demo with multiple tracks for different roles, industries, or company sizes.[Demo personalization at this level](https://www.storylane.io/blog/demo-personalization-software) means every prospect sees a version relevant to them, without your team needing to build and maintain a separate demo for each segment.
- **Transparent pricing, no hidden services costs.** Storylane's pricing is publicly listed. Support is included. There's no professional services dependency to maintain your own demo library.
- **Lead capture and CRM-connected analytics.** Know who watched your demo, how far they got, and where they dropped off. Route those signals directly to HubSpot or Salesforce so your sales team follows up on the right accounts at the right time.


Ready to move your demos over?[Start a free trial](https://app.storylane.io/signup) or[book a migration call](https://www.storylane.io/request-demo) to see how quickly your team can be up and running.
